speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me narrow down the cause, how long has this lesion been present, and has it changed in size or appearance recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum. The patient's presentation of a rapidly expanding, painful ulcerative lesion on the leg, combined with significant immunosuppression from corticosteroid treatment for anterior uveitis and the presence of Crohn's disease, strongly suggests a neutrophilic dermatosis like Pyoderma Gangrenosum. I recommend a skin biopsy to confirm the diagnosis and rule out infection or malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Skin_Biopsy; REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_differential; REQUEST IMAGES: Lesion_close_up.
